cards.text: This is a psalm of David, for the choirmaster, and David is talking straight to the LORD. He opens with this: "O LORD, You have searched me and known me." Searched AND known, friend, like somebody went through my old junk drawer and knew every rubber band by name.

cards.question: David says the LORD understands his thoughts, but only when David is close by.

cards.text: From afar, friend! The LORD knows when David sits and when he rises, and I can't even remember where I set my timer.

cards.question: David says the LORD searches out his path and his lying down, and is aware of ___ his ways.
David even talks about the words he says. When does he say the LORD knows all about them?

answers.text: Before a word is on his tongue

cards.text: The LORD hems David in, behind and before, and David says, "You have laid Your hand upon me." That's me packing a cookie box, mustache on both sides, NOTHING slipping out.

cards.question: The LORD knows David's every move and every word. What does David say about knowledge like that?

answers.text: It's too wonderful for him to reach
It's easy enough for him to explain
It's something he figured out long ago

cards.text: Then David asks, "Where can I go to escape Your Spirit? Where can I flee from Your presence?" Friend, I spent years at the back of a junk drawer, and I STILL got found.

cards.question: David says that if he went up to the heavens the LORD would be there, but if he made his bed in Sheol he'd finally be alone.

cards.text: Heavens or Sheol, the LORD is there both times. What if David rose on the wings of the dawn, or settled by the farthest sea?

cards.question: Way out by the farthest sea, what does David say the LORD's hand will do there?

answers.text: Guide him and hold him fast
Let go and let him wander

cards.text: One more hiding spot. What if David said the darkness would surely hide him, and the light would become night around him?

cards.question: David says that even the darkness is not dark to the LORD.

cards.text: In fact, "the night shines like the day, for darkness is as light to You." Meanwhile I can't find my apron with the lights ON.

Now David goes back to the very beginning: "For You formed my inmost being; You knit me together in my mother’s womb." Knit, friend, stitch by stitch, and I couldn't stamp one straight cookie for YEARS.

cards.question: Thinking about how the LORD made him, what does David do?

cards.text: David says, "I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made."

cards.question: David says that while he was made in secret, woven together in the depths of the earth, his frame was hidden from the LORD.
The LORD's eyes saw David's unformed body. And all his days, David says, were written in the LORD's ___ and ordained for him before one of them came to be.

cards.text: Then David says, "How precious to me are Your thoughts, O God, how vast is their sum!" Friend, I've got about two thoughts most mornings, and one of them is the oven timer.

cards.question: David says he could count up God's thoughts if he only had enough time.

cards.text: If he tried, David says, they would outnumber the grains of sand, "and when I awake, I am still with You."
Then the psalm takes a hard turn. David wishes God would slay the wicked, and he tells bloodthirsty men to get away from him.

cards.question: David wants those bloodthirsty men away from him. How does he describe them?
David asks, "Do I not hate those who hate You, O LORD, and detest those who rise against You?" How does he answer his own question?

answers.text: He hates them as his enemies

cards.question: After all that about God's enemies, David turns around and asks God to search HIM and know his heart.

cards.text: David prays, "Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my concerns." He opened by saying the LORD had searched him, and now he's ASKING for it, like a baker calling the inspector back on purpose.

cards.question: David asks God to see if there is any offensive way in him, and then to ___ him in the way everlasting.
